blue.limitations: The assessment of cardiac and mediastinal size and contour is limited by the two-dimensional nature of plain radiographs, which can be affected by patient positioning, phase of respiration, and body habitus. Detailed evaluation of specific cardiac chambers or mediastinal structures would require cross-sectional imaging. The images provided are standard chest radiographs, which have inherent limitations in fully characterizing subtle lung parenchymal abnormalities, especially in areas obscured by the heart or diaphragm. Overlying breast tissue can also create artifactual densities. Without prior imaging for comparison, it is difficult to determine the chronicity or progression of the observed reticular opacities. Further advanced imaging, such as CT, would be beneficial for a more detailed evaluation of the lung parenchyma.
